report: Reassessed the complete type-expression claim and its sole ordinary implementation and test association. Parser::type_expr constructs either a named path with optional arguments (empty when absent), or a tuple; type_list recursively calls type_expr for each argument or element, retaining the recursive TypeExpr tree without a fixed grammar nesting depth. The complete associated test parses Vec<(bool, Option<u32>)> and directly checks the outer name and arity, tuple length, bare bool with no arguments, inner Option name and arity, and bare u32 argument. These assertions account for both expression forms, optional generic arguments, nesting across both forms, and retention of that nesting; flattening or dropping an inner argument would fail them. Captured parse_body confirms it passes the supplied source into the reviewed parser with only a crate header added. No TODO/N/A entries or prerequisites apply. Independently verified current parser and full test source match the historical snapshots exactly and found the prior substantive rationale consistent with current claim and evidence. This is source inspection and exact comparison, not a test execution; only review start/read and comparison commands were run by this reviewer. Coordinator-reported suite/build results are separate evidence. No edits required.
